title: Frowning Face with Open Mouth Emoji 😦: What It Means
description: The frowning face with open mouth emoji 😦 is a jaw-drop with a frown: unpleasant surprise, dismay or disbelief. See how it differs from 😮 and 😧.
summary: The 😦 frowning face with open mouth shows a slack, downturned jaw and blank eyes. It means the sender has just heard something they did not like: an unpleasant surprise, a letdown, or news that leaves them speechless. It is quieter than a scream and less neutral than a simple gasp.
meaning: Picture the face someone makes when they open a parking ticket or hear that the concert is sold out. The mouth falls open, but the corners point down. That combination is what separates 😦 from the ordinary surprised faces: the shock is unwelcome. It says “oh... that's not good” more than “wow.”

Because the expression is so flat, it is not one of the popular emojis, and people who use it tend to mean it literally. It appears as a reaction to disappointing updates, awkward revelations and mildly disturbing facts. A friend explaining how hot dogs are made might get a single 😦 in return, and nothing else needs to be said.

It can also carry a note of offense or hurt. Sent after a blunt comment, it reads as “I can't believe you said that,” with the sender more wounded than angry. There is no established slang or ironic meaning attached to it, which makes it one of the more straightforward faces on the keyboard: what you see is roughly what the person feels.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It works best as a short reaction. Replying 😦 to “they canceled our flight” or “he's moving in with her already” tells the other person you are taken aback and waiting for more details. Adding it to your own bad news, as in “my card got declined 😦,” shows dismay without making a big production of it.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: In comment sections it turns up under unsettling trivia, unfortunate before-and-after photos and stories with a nasty twist. It is the mild, wordless alternative to typing “yikes.” Most platforms' reaction sets favor the more theatrical 😮 or 😱, so 😦 tends to be typed out by people who specifically want the frown.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is acceptable in informal chats when plans fall through, such as a meeting moved to Friday at five. Be careful using it in direct response to someone's work or decision, because a silent dismayed face reads as criticism and gives the other person nothing concrete to act on.

examples.text: The repair is going to cost HOW much 😦
examples.meaning: Unpleasant shock at a number far higher than expected.

examples.text: 😦 you told her I said that?
examples.meaning: Dismayed and a little hurt that a confidence was shared.

examples.text: Just found out the restaurant closed for good 😦
examples.meaning: Surprised disappointment at losing a favorite place.
The sinking realization of having gotten something wrong.

examples.text: He ate the whole cake before the party 😦

combos.meaning: Dismay that deepens into real distress as the news sinks in.
Shock at an unexpected cost or a drained bank account.
Stunned at first, then angry once the surprise wears off.

confusedWith.difference: 😧 is the same open frown with raised, worried eyebrows added, which pushes it toward pain or alarm. 😦 has no eyebrows on most platforms and looks blanker, more stunned than suffering.
😮 has a round, neutral mouth and can be used for good surprises. 😦 pulls the mouth corners down, so the surprise it shows is always a bad or uncomfortable one.
😯 has a small mouth and raised brows, suggesting quiet, impressed surprise. 😦 is wider and unhappier, closer to dismay than to being quietly amazed.

avoid: Do not send it alone in reply to someone's creative work, outfit or idea; it looks like you are appalled.
It is too mild for tragic news, where it can seem like you barely reacted.
Avoid it when you are pleasantly surprised, since the frown signals the opposite.
design: A yellow face with plain oval eyes and an open mouth whose corners turn downward. Apple, Google and most other vendors draw it without eyebrows, which gives it a vacant, stunned quality and is the easiest way to tell it apart from the anguished face. Small sizes make the two nearly indistinguishable, which is one reason neither is widely used.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😦 and 😧?
faqs.a: Eyebrows. 😧 has raised, slanted brows that make it look pained or frightened. 😦 usually has none, so it reads as blank dismay. In practice people use them almost interchangeably for bad surprises.
It is more shocked than sad. The frown shows the surprise is unwelcome, but there are no tears or drooping eyes. For actual sadness, 😞 or 😢 communicate it more clearly.

It can. When it follows a rude or tactless remark, it usually means the person is taken aback and possibly hurt. If you get one after a joke, it is worth checking that the joke landed the way you intended.

faqs.q: When was the frowning face with open mouth added?
faqs.a: It was included in Emoji 1.0, the first official emoji list, in 2015, though the character itself was already available on major phones before that list was published.
